title: Kauaʻian Honeymoon
headline: Two weeks on the Garden Isle
subtitle: Mixing luxury and hiking and camping in one of the most beautiful places in the world

overview.lede: We had two things we absolutely wanted: to hike the Kalalau Trail and sleep on the beach at the end of it, and to see Waimea Canyon. Both needed permits months ahead. They sit on opposite sides of Kauaʻi.
body: These naturally bookended the trip - alternating between roughing it and luxury accommodations. That rhythm turned out to make everything better. It is so much easier to shoulder a pack again after a few days of full stomachs and clean sheets and they are appreciated more after roughing it.

Fly into Lihu'e, rent an open top Jeep, and drive up to the Kalalau Trail, Hanalei Bay, then across the island to Waimea Canyon for more camping and hiking at 3,000 ft, then down to the south coast of Po'ipu for some final pampering.
The photographs, memories, and adventures are ours.
overview.mapCaption: Two permits, opposite ends of the island. The road between them is the whole trip.
overview.mapAlt: Map of Kauaʻi: the ring road from the Kalalau trailhead round to Waimea Canyon, and the seven places we stopped

chapters.title: Kalalau Trail
chapters.note: Eleven miles in along the Nāpali Coast, two nights on the sand at the end of it, and eleven miles back out.
chapters.mapAlt: The Kalalau Trail from the Keʻe trailhead along the Nāpali Coast to Kalalau Beach, with night one's camp above Hanakāpīʻai

activities.title: Trailhead to Hanakapia Falls
activities.description: Our flight came in too late to make it to the first campsite so we did a quick overnight near the airport.  Early the next morning we drive north towards the trailhead.  We make a quick stop at the Surfboard House, our accommodations after the trail to drop off what we wouldn't need - Simon was glad to oblige.  It's recommended to leave nothing in your vehicle at the trailhead and to leave it open.

chapters.title: Surfboard House
chapters.note: A bed, a full kitchen, and the bay a block away. We kayaked the coast we had just walked.
chapters.mapAlt: The north shore of Kauaʻi, with Hanalei marked

chapters.title: Waimea Canyon
chapters.note: Back into the tent, three thousand feet up. Swamp boardwalk one day, a cliff trail over the sea the next.
chapters.mapAlt: The Kōkeʻe plateau above Waimea Canyon: our campsite, and the three days of walking from it — the Alakaʻi out and back, the west-rim loop, and down into the canyon

chapters.title: Poʻipū
chapters.note: Head to the South beach for some much needed pampering.

planning.headline: Three rules, and a lot of driving
planning.intro: Sixteen days is long enough to get greedy. What kept this trip good was deciding early what we would not do.
planning.nightsNote: Alternating the two mattered more than any single thing we did.
planning.timeBudgetNote: Hours across the trip by category, totalled from the itinerary itself — the goal was a full trip with real unstructured time left in it, not a schedule with no room to breathe.

principles.title: Develop around a few must haves first and plan around them
principles.description: We wanted to do the Kalalau trail and camp at the beach.  We also wanted to camp and hike Waimea canyon.  Both of those required permits from the state with ample lead time.  These activities were on opposite sides of the island by road, so this lead to a natural path between the two.

principles.title: Alternate between roughing it in the tent and luxury accomodations
principles.description: So much easier to do that second camping trip after a few days in a comfortable bed with a full stomach.

principles.title: Be honest with yourself about your level of effort and number of activities
principles.description: We knew we could handle the hikes and the camping.  I still left room in the schedule for spontaneous decisions, like our visit to Kauai Coffee and swimming at Ho'opi'i Falls.
